chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Three things make the private part permissible: marriage with inheritance, marriage without inheritance, and marriage by ownership of the right hand.

key_terms.الْفَرْجَ: The private part (referring to sexual intimacy)
key_terms.بِمِلْكِ الْيَمِينِ: By ownership of the right hand (concubinage)
key_terms.نِكَاحٌ بِلَا مِيرَاثٍ: Temporary marriage (mut'ah, which does not include inheritance)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of marriage that permit intimacy in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* categorizes the three legal avenues for permissible intimacy, explicitly distinguishing between permanent (*daim*) and temporary (*mut'ah*) marriages alongside concubinage (*milk al-yamin*). It reflects the foundational Shia juristic view that these three modes constitute the complete set of lawful relations, with the inclusion of *nikah bil-la mirath* serving as the primary evidence for the validity of *Mut'ah* in Shia fiqh. The narration underscores the structural clarity of Shia marriage law by grouping these distinct contractual forms under a single legal principle of permissibility.
